prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its active form, which made incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: After the full exchange I still hold B014 as a single-achievement prize, and the round-1 files strengthen that view because all six of us give the same scientific reasons independently of the opening result. The chain from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1 to identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and then to drugs with randomized evidence in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes is complete, has been confirmed for decades, and is mature. The chair's first question, whether to anchor the citation on physiology alone or on physiology plus therapy, is the real hinge. My answer is physiology and the active peptide, with the therapies named as the consequence and not as a credited achievement. That anchor makes the third laureate Mojsov. The citation I propose still states that the work enabled incretin-based treatment, so the clinical outcome is recognised without asking the committee to adjudicate between pharmaceutical programmes.
statement.case_against: Credit remains the weakness and I cannot make it fully fair. Whichever name is left out, Knudsen or Mojsov, has a legitimate claim, and the early proglucagon and GLP-1 work of the Habener group lies outside the credited names. I also accept that a prize anchored on the active peptide may be read as under-crediting the step that turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug. A further risk is that my preferred reading depends on a priority record for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide that several of us, myself included, can only partly verify from the supplied materials. If that record were shown to favour others clearly, my third seat would be weaker.

responses.point: Per proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen so that the prize spans mechanism through to the drug, and as chair he asks whether the third seat depends on how the citation is anchored.
responses.response: I agree that the third seat follows from the anchor and I think that is the most useful way to frame the disagreement. Your trio is coherent if the committee decides the prize should explicitly reward the development of long-acting agonists. I remain on the other side because identification of the active peptide is a discovery contribution with no substitute, whereas analogue engineering optimises a known molecule inside a company programme. I have not changed my configuration, but I would move if the committee concluded that a physiology-only citation leaves the clinical achievement unrecognised, and I note you yourself call the Mojsov trio defensible. I would not call this three-three split a matter of support counts, it is a disagreement about what the prize honours.

responses.point: Rickard backs Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, calls the allocation a real difficulty, and says the trio gets harder to defend if therapy must be rewarded explicitly. He also would not resist a Knudsen configuration strongly.
responses.response: I agree with both the trio and your honest caveat. Your point that Knudsen's step was a creative scientific achievement and not merely industrial is fair and I withdraw any implication in my round-1 wording that it was incremental in a pejorative sense. Where I still differ from a Knudsen reading is narrower: it would require the citation to credit drug development, and I prefer that the clinical consequence appears as the result of the discovery. Your caveat is also my own, so I would test the trio against the citation wording and not against opening rankings.

responses.point: Thomas favours Holst, Drucker and Mojsov, asks that the primary priority literature be checked before the final ballot, and warns that B039 is a less clean fallback than its opening rank suggests.
responses.response: I share your concern about the priority record and, since we cannot settle it from the materials supplied, I would word the citation around the physiology and the active form of GLP-1 and not around a first-identification claim, which also deals with the Habener question in the chair's third prompt. I agree with your qualification on B039: Eshhar's concept is outside the credited names and the position of Rosenberg is uncertain, so I would not assume CAR-T is an automatic next choice. That is why I now treat B003 and B039 as alternatives with different weaknesses, credit versus clinical maturity, and not as a ranked pair.

responses.point: Abdel takes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, emphasising that long-acting analogues made the therapy practical and that no three-person configuration is clean, and he ranks the unfolded protein response as a strong alternative.
responses.response: I agree that no clean three-person answer exists and that the translational chain is unusually clear. I disagree on weight: the long-acting analogue is important, but a discovery prize most defensibly rests on the physiology that made the analogue conceivable. On a two-part prize, I considered pairing B014 with B003 as the chair's fourth prompt suggests, and I would not do that. The GLP-1 achievement already contains the basic-to-clinical arc, a second part would dilute it, and it would not resolve the third-laureate question. I keep B003 as an alternative because the Walter and Mori credit is the most compact on the shortlist.

uncertainties: Whether the primary record establishes who identified and first characterised the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and how that weighs against the Habener group's early proglucagon work.
Whether the committee wants the citation anchored on physiology alone or on physiology plus therapy, which decides between Mojsov and Knudsen for the third seat.
Whether the cited long-term durability and safety of incretin effects in obesity is complete enough to leave out of the citation wording, although I regard it as not a maturity barrier.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. No specific conflict is apparent for the shortlisted candidates. My field of autoimmunity and rheumatology is adjacent to CAR-T applications in autoimmune disease (B039, an alternative only), and I hold a group-leader affiliation at Bergen, but I have no documented tie to any credited person and I infer none.
